recommendation.title: Easy medium-long, stay disciplined
recommendation.reasoning: TSB has dipped to -17.76 (crossing the reduced-intensity threshold) after yesterday's long run, whose MP finish saw HR climb to 172-174bpm in the last ~10 minutes, above the 167bpm LT. That reads as normal cardiac drift rather than a red flag -- the segment came after ~55 minutes of running (not fresh legs), it was the athlete's first time at this exact pace, and RPE wasn't maximal (room to hold ~10 more minutes), all classic signs of drift rather than a true threshold-limiting effort. Worth a light check at Aug 13's fresher-legs MP reps rather than acting on it now. HRV is essentially at baseline (70ms vs 71ms, -1%, balanced) and resting HR (44bpm) is normal, both fine, but sleep was middling (6.6h, score 67) after an already-short night before. Tomorrow's session is already prescribed as easy effort, so no session swap is needed -- just hold it genuinely easy.
recommendation.sessionDetail: 35 minutes at easy effort (~75-85% LT ≈ 125-142bpm) -- moved from Monday, last easy session before tonight's Flixbus to Oslo. Keep this one honestly easy: yesterday's long run drifted toward the top of the easy band before the MP finish even started, so build in a slower start if HR climbs early.

sessions.lesson: Long-run prescription (70min: easy body + MP finish) executed close to plan at 66.5min/12.21km, and the MP segment actually happened (~10 of the planned 15 min at ~4:20/km per the athlete) rather than being downgraded -- HR climbed to 172-174bpm in that closing segment, above the 167bpm LT itself, but that reads as normal cardiac drift after ~55 minutes of running plus first exposure to this pace rather than a too-hard effort: RPE wasn't maximal (athlete had ~10 more minutes in the tank). The easy-effort body of the run also crept to 140-147bpm in its second half rather than holding 125-142bpm throughout, consistent with the same late-run drift.

Duration was right on the 45-minute prescription, but HR drifted from ~135bpm in the first half to 148-153bpm in the final 10 minutes -- likely fatigue-driven drift (short sleep, deep TSB) rather than a pace change.

This wasn't the skipped Sunday run -- 92.7 minutes at a moderate-but-non-running HR (avg 102, mostly 85-120bpm) suggests background movement, consistent with the plan's own call to skip today's run given -29.4 TSB and HRV 24% below baseline at the time.

8.75 hours at a very low, steady HR (mostly 75-95bpm) -- not a training session, this was the Greenfield Festival day, and because hrTSS scales with duration alone it produced this block's single biggest TSS number (227) despite negligible real running stress.

This is the reduced long run pulled forward from Saturday -- pace and duration were on target (8.31km/47min) but HR climbed to 154-166bpm in the final 5 minutes (a fast finish), pushing the average to 139bpm, at/above the top of the easy band rather than staying easy throughout.
Easy run + strides -- the HR spikes to 148-156bpm in the last 8 minutes are exactly what accelerations should look like, brief and at the end, not a sign the easy portion ran hot.

Ran almost double the prescribed 25-30 minutes (53.8min) -- worth checking whether that was intentional extra aerobic work, since swim HR doesn't map directly onto the run-based zone thresholds anyway.

recentActivity.analysis: TSS this week is now correctly cleaned of two big outliers -- Aug 1's festival day (227 TSS) and Aug 2's background movement (57.6 TSS) no longer count as training load -- leaving five real training days with a normal progressive pattern (55 -> 41 -> 55 -> 54 -> 84 TSS, swim/easy/easy/easy/long). Jul 31's and Aug 4's 'easy' portions both drifted into the upper-140s late in the run, and today's MP finish spiked to 172-174bpm above LT -- most likely ordinary cardiac drift late in longer efforts (Jul 31 was a fast finish, Aug 4's MP segment came after ~55 minutes with RPE still short of maximal) rather than a pacing problem, but worth a light check whether the same pattern shows up on a fresher-legs quality day like Aug 13's MP reps.
